title: The two branches of a nodal family form an etale double cover of its singular subscheme
statement:
Let $f:X\to T$ be a flat locally finitely presented morphism of schemes such that every nonempty geometric fibre is equidimensional of dimension one and its nonsmooth points have completed local rings $\Omega[[u,v]]/(uv)$ over their algebraically closed residue fields. Put $D=\operatorname{Sing}(f)$, the closed subscheme defined by the first Fitting ideal of $\Omega^1_{X/T}$ [def-trf-first-fitting-singular-subscheme]. There is a canonical finite etale morphism $p:B_f\to D$ of degree two (that is, $p_*\mathcal O_{B_f}$ is locally free of rank two). For each $t\in T$, let $X_t^\nu\to X_t$ denote the normalization of the reduced fibre. There is a canonical isomorphism of $D_t$-schemes
$$ (B_f)_t\ \cong\ X_t^\nu\times_{X_t}D_t. $$
The scheme $D_t$ is reduced and its points are exactly the nonsmooth points of $X_t$. The two geometric points of $B_f$ over a geometric point of $D$ are its two geometric normalization branches. The construction is functorial under isomorphisms of families and under every base change $a:T'\to T$: writing $f':X\times_TT'\to T'$ one has canonical identifications $D_{f'}=D\times_TT'$ and $B_{f'}=B_f\times_TT'$ compatible with $p$ and with composition of base changes. If $f$ is finitely presented, both $D_t$ and $(B_f)_t$ are finite etale over $\kappa(t)$. If, in addition, $f$ is proper, then $D\to T$ and $B_f\to T$ are finite.

Flatness, local finite presentation, geometric fibres, smoothness, dimension, completion, power series, normalization, fibre products, finite morphisms, etaleness and properness are [def-weil-flat-morphism], [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation], [def-weil-geometric-fibre], [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms], [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension], [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion], [def-weil-pbc-multivariate-power-series], [def-weil-pbc-reduced-normalization], [def-pc-fibre-product], [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism], [def-weil-etale-morphism] and [def-weil-proper-morphism]. Residue fields are [def-weil-residue-field].

proof.text: By [lem-trf-nodal-family-fitting-singular], $D$ is the nonsmooth locus, is unramified over $T$, and commutes with arbitrary base change. Apply [lem-trf-unramified-field-fibre-decomposition] to each fibre: $D_t=\coprod_x\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(x)$ with $\kappa(x)/\kappa(t)$ finite separable. Thus $D_t$ is reduced with exactly the required points.

Use [lem-sfb-graph-cone-gluing] for $i:D\hookrightarrow X$: it constructs $\mathcal G_f$ and identifies $B_f=\operatorname{Proj}_D\mathcal G_f$ with the fixed graph exceptional fibre, canonically under family isomorphisms.

By [lem-sfb-nodal-graph-cone-chart], an etale cover $D_U\to D$ identifies the pulled-back graded algebra with $\mathcal O_{D_U}[u,v]/(uv)$. Flat Proj base change [prop-nagata-relative-proj-functoriality] computes the cover of $B_f$. On $D_+(u)$, $v=0$ and the degree-zero ring is $A$; on $D_+(v)$ it is $A$; their intersection is empty since $uv=0$ [def-nagata-affine-proj]. Hence it is $D_U\amalg D_U$. Descend degree two by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-locally-free-degree-etale-descent] and etaleness by [lem-weil-pbc-fpqc-finer-than-etale], [lem-galois-fpqc-descend-etale]. The rank assertion is [lem-pc-flf-properties].

proof.text: For $T'=\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(t)$, apply [lem-sfb-nodal-graph-cone-fibre] to the fibre family and use Step 4. Its graph-cone identification gives $(B_f)_t\cong X_t^\nu\times_{X_t}D_t$ and identifies the two geometric points with the two normalization branches.

source.place: Tags 0CBT (remark-quadratic-extension), 0CBU and 0CBW; Algebra formally etale localization and separable field maps.

proof.text: If $f$ is finitely presented it is quasi-compact [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation]; $D_t$ is closed, hence quasi-compact [lem-weil-pbc-closed-in-quasi-compact]. Its disjoint open points therefore form a finite set. Their finite separable fields make $D_t$ finite etale [lem-exc-etale-coproduct-etale]. Apply [lem-trf-unramified-field-fibre-decomposition] to the finite etale cover over each such field. Separability is transitive [lem-zl-separable-permanence], so $(B_f)_t$ is also a finite coproduct of separable field spectra; finiteness uses [lem-weil-pbc-finite-composition].

source.place: Tags 0C59 and 0CBT; Morphisms 02G7 (lemma-unramified-over-field), quasi-compact discrete decomposition.

proof.text: If $f$ is proper, $D\to T$ is proper [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-proper] and has discrete finite fibres by Steps 1 and 6. It is quasi-finite [pqf-def-quasifinite], hence finite [cor-pqf-proper-quasifinite-finite]. Composing with finite $p$ gives finite $B_f\to T$ [lem-weil-pbc-finite-composition].
